A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EpiNode study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic and surveillance-data forecasting experiments, failure-mode demonstrations, parameter-recovery results, and ablations.

after.justification: V2 reports original forecasting, peak-error, parameter-recovery, regional, and ablation results, including revised numerical comparisons.

M1.justification: V1 Algorithm 1 decomposes the full infection series into forecasting controls. V2 restricts VMD to training observations and introduces forecast-window controls using linear trend extrapolation, seasonal repetition, and the training residual mean. This changes the forecasting procedure and its access to future information; the latent ODEs, SIRS dynamics, and observation loss remain.

E1.justification: V2 removes the COVID-like illness symptoms dataset and its results throughout the paper and appendices, eliminating the only real-world non-seasonal disease benchmark. The four synthetic settings and ILI data from ten HHS regions remain.

E2.justification: The peak-error comparison expands from v1 Figure 10 to v2 Figures 10/A4 and Tables A3/A4 by adding LSTM, EINN-SEIRm, NeuralODE, and KAN-ODEs. These methods already participated in v1 forecasting comparisons. TimeKAN and TimeMixer++ remain evaluated in v2 figures despite being omitted from its new numerical tables.

E3.justification: Training-only decomposition replaces full-series preprocessing, substantially changing forecast information availability. The illustrated SIR peak comparison changes from split 0.2 in v1 Figure 10 to 0.1 in v2 Figure A4. V2 also revises the stated metric specification and describes aggregation across multiple splits, although its relationship to the figures showing individual splits remains unclear; this does not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 removes CLS-specific architecture, component-count, decomposition-method, and time-delay ablation evidence from v1 Figure 14, retaining these questions on five settings in Figure A9. Appendix F explicitly discusses split-placement robustness, without providing separate scores for each split. Regional and physics-mismatch analyses remain.

E5.justification: V1 states that results are averaged over multiple seeds but provides no corresponding standard deviations. V2 introduces mean-and-standard-deviation tables, benchmark and ablation error bars, peak-error uncertainty, and parameter-trajectory bands. Neither version specifies seed counts, so an increase in repetitions is not established.

E6.justification: Benchmark values, peak errors, inferred trajectories, and ablation rankings change extensively. ILI EpiNode RMSE changes from approximately 0.006 in v1 Figure 9f to 0.0093 in v2 Table 1, while the strongest plotted baseline changes from LSTM to TimeMixer++; these are not established same-protocol comparisons. For varying-parameter SIRS, three components cease to be best: v2 Figure A9b reports approximately 0.009 for two components versus 0.019 for three. Wavelet also replaces VMD as the best decomposition there.

T1.justification: V2 Equations 9–11 introduce mathematical definitions for trend extrapolation, periodic seasonal extension, and residual continuation beyond the observation window. The existing VMD/ADMM and SIRS mathematics remain substantially unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The main applicability claim narrows from seasonal and non-seasonal diseases to seasonal epidemics, although the new Impact Statement retains the broader assertion. The abstract replaces the earlier 15–35% RMSE reduction and 1–3-week peak-timing improvement with a 27–70% reduction against the strongest baseline and best peak-detection accuracy across five datasets.

C2.justification: V2 substantially qualifies parameter interpretation: recovery rate is described as the model's preferred decomposition of effective reproduction dynamics rather than a direct recovery-rate estimate. It adds double-peak smoothing as a single-strain SIRS limitation, dependence on preprocessing choices, and an explanation for the two-component advantage on varying-parameter SIRS. V1's more general uncertainty and spatial limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds frequency-based mode grouping, delay-offset alignment, and seasonal-period fallbacks to Algorithm 1. Appendices F/H disclose split grids and dataset-specific hyperparameter tuning, but not selected hyperparameter values or training budgets. The stated implementation location changes from an anonymous 4open.science repository to a named GitHub repository.

R1.justification: V2 adds forecasting references supporting channel extrapolation, including Harvey, Cleveland and colleagues, Bloomfield, Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, and Zeng and colleagues. Additional epidemic-modeling references support the new multi-strain and identifiability discussion. The central positioning relative to neural ODEs and mechanistic hybrids remains.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative, moving regional analyses, ablation results, and the baseline-capability comparison into appendices. Results and conclusion passages are rewritten, new appendix sections explain splits and tuning, and acknowledgements and an Impact Statement are added.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, redraws the framework diagram, and adds numerical benchmark, split, and peak-error tables. Benchmark and peak plots are redistributed between main text and appendices, while ablation displays gain numerical labels and uncertainty bars. Numerous retained figures are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 Algorithm 1 replaces full-series controls with training-only decomposition and explicit forecast extensions, addressing future-information leakage in v1's procedure as written. This substantial correction, broader uncertainty reporting, and the recovery-rate identifiability caveat strengthen validity and interpretation. Removing CLS narrows validation, and v2 misattributes KAN-ODEs/EARTH scores to TimeKAN/TimeMixer++ in Section 4.5.1 while leaving split aggregation ambiguous. These reporting weaknesses limit confidence in the advertised gains but do not outweigh the procedural and interpretive improvements.
